answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks by anchoring identities to optical physical unclonable functions. Verifiers project light through a prism onto an agent's quartz wafer, deriving keys from speckle patterns formed by each microscopic ridge. An attacker cannot emulate these unclonable physics in software and must purchase discrete physical tokens for every alias. However, thermal drift can alter optical alignments and falsely reject valid agents.
